hypotheses.title: Deploy v184 connection-pool refactor regressed connection handling
hypotheses.summary: The v184 rollout finished at 14:28 and refactored database connection pool acquisition; pool saturation and the HTTP 500 spike followed within minutes.
unknowns: Whether the v184 pool refactor changed acquisition semantics without changing max_connections
validation_steps: Diff v183..v184 for the connection pool acquisition changes
Replay v184 under a staging load test and watch pool saturation

impact_claims.description: HTTP 500 errors reached 22% of requests on checkout and cart endpoints

remediation_items.description: Roll back to v183 and re-test the pool acquisition refactor behind a canary

hypotheses.title: Primary connection pool was undersized for the offered load
hypotheses.summary: The primary pool saturated at 40 connections with growing pending waits, and raising the limit to 80 cleared the errors, pointing at capacity rather than the deploy.
unknowns: Whether request volume at 14:31 exceeded the pre-deploy baseline
validation_steps: Compare request volume and pool saturation before and after 14:28

impact_claims.description: Database connection acquisition waits exceeded 3 seconds during the incident

remediation_items.description: Size pool max_connections from measured concurrency and alert on sustained pending waits

hypotheses.title: An upstream dependency degraded during the window
hypotheses.summary: An upstream dependency may have degraded and driven the errors, but none of the collected artifacts evidence this.
unknowns: Whether any uninspected dependency degraded between 14:28 and 14:40
validation_steps: Check status pages and metrics for each upstream dependency across 14:28-14:40
